question: What is the SI unit of 'volume'?
solution:
The correct answer is __Cubic meter**(m³)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cubic meter (m³)__ is the SI unit of volume.
 
• It is defined as the volume of a cube with sides of 1 meter in length.
 
• The cubic meter is used to measure the volume of materials or spaces in various applications such as construction and fluid measurement.
 
• It is equivalent to 1000 liters or 1,000,000 cubic centimeters.
 
• The cubic meter is widely used in scientific, engineering, and industrial contexts for standardized volume measurement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Other commonly used units of volume:**

 
 
• **Liter:** A non-SI unit used for measuring volumes, especially liquids. 1 liter = 0.001 cubic meter.
 
• **Milliliter:** A smaller unit of volume, commonly used in laboratories. 1 milliliter = 0.001 liter.
 
• **Cubic centimeter:** Equivalent to 1 milliliter and used in various scientific applications.
